prompt: Create a printable-looking recipe page for 'Smoked Lentil Stew' from the Hollis Farm Kitchen. Ingredients: 1.5 cups brown lentils, 1 smoked paprika tbsp, 2 carrots, 1 onion, 4 cups stock, 2 tbsp olive oil, salt. Method has five steps (sauté onion and carrot, add paprika, add lentils and stock, simmer 35 min, season and rest 10 min). Include a nutrition panel with calories 310, protein 17 g, carbs 46 g, fat 7 g, fiber 14 g per serving. Deliver a single self-contained HTML file with inline CSS, system fonts only, and no external assets.
rubric: Body text is comfortable to read: sized for reading and with generous line spacing.
Line length for the method text is limited rather than spanning a wide window.
Nutrition values line up so digits can be compared down the column.
Headings are distinguishable from body by size or weight in a restrained set of steps.
Spacing between paragraphs and sections is consistent and clearly larger above headings than below.

prompt: Review this CSS for the article body of our hospital newsletter: body {font: 12px/1.1 Arial; color:#999; max-width: none; text-align: justify;} h2 {font-size: 13px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing:0;} p {margin:0 0 4px;}. Readers say it's tiring to read. List the problems and give a corrected version.
rubric: Flags the body size as too small for comfortable reading and gives a larger value.
Flags the tight line height and suggests a roomier one.
Flags low contrast gray text and improves it.
Flags unlimited line length and gives a constraint.
Flags justification without hyphenation or the cramped paragraph spacing, and fixes it.
Provides runnable replacement CSS.

prompt: Improve the typography of this invoice summary without changing its content. HTML: a table with rows Item / Qty / Unit / Total, three line items (Pallet wrap rolls, 12, $8.40, $100.80; Strapping kit, 3, $42.00, $126.00; Dock labels, 40, $0.35, $14.00), then Subtotal $240.80, Tax (8%) $19.26, Total due $260.06. Return an HTML file with inline CSS and system fonts, no external assets.
rubric: Money amounts are right-aligned or otherwise aligned so decimals line up.
Numbers use a consistent number of decimal places.
Total due is distinguished from subtotal and tax with weight or size.
Column headers are visually distinct yet quiet.
The type scale is small and consistent, with no more than a handful of sizes.

prompt: Why do some timers and scoreboards in apps jitter horizontally as the digits change, and what should we do about it? Our game shows time as 12:48.3 updating every 100ms and scores like 1,204 and 998.
rubric: Explains that proportional-width digits change width and shift neighbors.
Recommends a concrete fix such as tabular numerals or a fixed-width treatment.
Gives an actual code snippet or property name.
Mentions that the fix should apply to all changing numbers (scores too).
Stays practical for the stated game scenario.

prompt: We're picking the body text setup for a long-form help center for a tax-prep tool. Option 1: 15px, line-height 1.4, container 1100px wide. Option 2: 18px, line-height 1.6, container 680px wide. Option 3: 16px, line-height 1.3, two columns each 480px. Which do you pick and why?
rubric: Chooses one option clearly, with Option 2 or equally defensible reasoning.
Connects line length or measure to readability.
Connects size and line height to comfortable reading.
Explains a downside of at least one rejected option.
Suggests one tweak (e.g. responsive reduction on small screens).

prompt: Design a dark-mode quarterly summary card for a savings app, Nestwell. Show: 'Q3 summary' title, Interest earned $182.47, Deposits $2,400.00, Withdrawals $310.00, Ending balance $14,962.18, and a note 'Rates may change. See terms.' Deliver a single self-contained HTML file with inline CSS, system fonts only, and no external assets.
rubric: Light text on the dark background is not pure harsh white on pure black, and has comfortable contrast.
Text on dark is not too thin or tiny.
The amounts align in a column with consistent decimals.
Ending balance is differentiated from the other lines.
The note is smaller but still legible.

prompt: Fix the typography of this event flyer text as a single HTML page: 'THE HARBOR NIGHT MARKET' as the title, 'Fridays, May-September -- 5pm to 11pm' as a subtitle, a paragraph of about 50 words that you write about food stalls, live music and local makers, and 'Free entry - Pier 9 - Dogs welcome' as the footer. Use proper dashes and quotes where needed. Inline CSS, system fonts, no external assets.
rubric: Dash usage is typographically correct for the date range (en dash) and parenthetical punctuation.
All-caps text, if used, has some added letter spacing, and long running text is not all caps.
There is a clear title, subtitle, body and footer hierarchy using few sizes.
Body paragraph is a readable size with comfortable line height.
Alignment is consistent and not justified without reason.

prompt: Our designer says every number in our dashboard tables should use a different font setting than the headings. I think that's overkill. Who's right? We show prices, ETAs in minutes and counts.
rubric: Takes a clear position and supports it.
Explains that digit alignment matters when numbers are compared in columns.
Distinguishes numbers that need alignment from numbers in running prose.
Gives a concrete implementation direction.
Avoids dogmatism.

prompt: Quick sanity check, tell me if there's anything wrong with this and fix it only if needed: article {font: 17px/1.6 system-ui; max-width: 66ch; margin: 0 auto;} article h2 {font-size: 1.5rem; margin: 2rem 0 .5rem;} article p {margin: 0 0 1rem;}
rubric: Recognizes the CSS is already sound and says so.
Does not manufacture major changes.
If suggesting anything, offers only minor optional refinements.
Keeps the answer short.

prompt: For our airline's flight-status board, someone proposes using a monospace font for the whole thing 'so numbers line up'. The board shows destination cities, flight numbers, gate, status text and departure time. Is that a good idea? Pick an approach.
rubric: Gives a clear verdict and does not endorse monospace everywhere just for alignment.
Proposes aligned numerals only on numeric columns or an equivalent targeted approach.
Considers that city names and status text read better in a normal text face.
Offers a concrete CSS-level suggestion.
